models_evaluated: Flexible-horizon ML model (NACC Uniform Data Set, 20 inputs, HORIZON feature)

links.outcome: Flexible-horizon ML model versus Cox proportional hazards baseline: G-mean, sensitivity, specificity
links.effect: ML had higher G-mean at four of five horizons and higher specificity from 48 months; Cox had greater sensitivity from 48 months onwards.
links.quote: Compared with a Cox proportional hazards model, our flexible-horizon ML model achieved a higher G-mean at four of the five evaluated horizons and higher specificity from 48 months onwards, whereas Cox achieved greater sensitivity from 48 months onwards.

links.outcome: Model discrimination across sex, race and age subgroups (exploratory)
links.effect: Broadly similar balanced discrimination across sex, race and age groups, although sensitivity-specificity trade-offs varied.
links.quote: Exploratory subgroup analyses showed broadly similar balanced discrimination across sex, race and age groups, although sensitivity-specificity trade-offs varied.

screen.reason: The study develops and retrospectively evaluates a flexible-horizon predictive risk model for dementia detection, including fairness and explainability analyses, but does not test a specific deployment practice or safeguard.
